newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends down 0.02 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends down 0.02 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real closed down 0.02 percent at 1.0306 per greenback on dollar inflows in calm trading on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Nearly $200 million was injected in the market today ahead of the payment for shares of Rio de Janeiro power utility Cerj, which was privatized on Wednesday.
Banco Interatlantico brokered the sale of the dollars, representing Portuguese firm EDP, who acquired, along with Chile's Chilectra and Spain's Endesa, a majority stake in Cerj, a bank source said.
The central bank bought dollars at 1.0305 per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market in the late afternoon.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Friday surplus of $75 million.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0361 per dollar, up 0.01 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.095 real per greenback.
